data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2022 gross claims outstanding were GBP 253.397m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates a net adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 21.8m (about 8.6% of opening gross reserves), driven by adverse development in several older underwriting years (notably 2019 and 2020) partially offset by favourable development in other years. Causes cited in the report include frequent natural catastrophe activity, higher claim costs driven by inflation, model shortcomings and geopolitical events; named events referenced include Hurricane Ian and multiple Japanese typhoons which have influenced reserve and currency dynamics.
raw_causal_phrases: 2022 was an eventful year, with both geopolitical and natural catastrophes dominating the insurance landscape.
The war in Ukraine and Hurricane Ian are both substantial but manageable events for the Syndicate

a combination of the frequent, severe natural catastrophes seen in recent years, high inflation coupled with a tightening of monetary policy by central banks, increased loss costs driving increased demand and a failure of catastrophe models to recognise this
Hurricane Ian which, as the second largest insured loss in history after Hurricane Katrina, drove 2022 to become the 5th worst recorded loss year in history.
heightened catastrophic activity and the impact of COVID-19
In terms of COVID-19 claims, management have considered all policies exposed and potential coverages.
The currency shortfall in Japanese Yen is partly driven by the gross claims for Typhoons Hagibis, Faxai and Jebi being mainly in Japanese Yen
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (PYD) has been calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross figures) because no explicit single-line 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding (gross)' was found in the notes. The triangle method excludes the two most recent underwriting years per the methodology. The report includes RITC/closed year transfers (2020 closed by RITC) and named catastrophe events which can distort development patterns; PYD therefore has moderate confidence (0.8). Exact textual description of a gross prior-year movement was not located, so exact_reserve_text is blank.
